speech_style: Speak in conversational Philippine English as a warm, expressive community health storyteller. Pronounce Mimi MEE-mee. Let her proposal sound curious and practical; emphasize one small review step, service needs and agreed follow-up with deliberate gentle pauses. Vary pitch and pace naturally while keeping one consistent narrator timbre. Read exactly the authored words, without fillers, invented approval or promises. End clearly and encouragingly.

beats.text: Mimi confirms another activity is planned in the meeting area. The reminder of who checks the schedule is unclear. How could one small suggestion help?
State the factual concern and confirmed schedule. No blame, patient data or invented savings. Separate what is known from what is still unknown.
Mimi proposes reviewing whether a short meeting-end checklist is needed. Check the existing process first. This is a proposal, not an instruction to implement immediately.
The reason: clearer schedule checks and handover. Verify time, materials and service needs. Mimi does not promise approval, repairs or a savings amount.
Confirm responsibility and authority. Agree who will review, what to check and when to speak again. Review first; no new checklist while a decision is pending.
Practice: a concern, one proposal and reason, local checks and follow-up. Protect service. Workplace skill is observed separately; online completion alone is insufficient.
